Inspection 2 Findings:
R380-80-3(1): Provider is responsible for their own staff's compliance | Finding: The provider was out of compliance with R380-80-3(1) for failing to comply with each applicable federal, state, and local law, and each policy and administrative rule required by the department or by other state and federal agencies that regulate or oversee the provider’s programs. Investigative interviews indicate that the provider enforced restrictive calling policies that unlawfully blocked client communication with the Ombuds office. While the Ombudsman contact details were physically posted on-site, clients were not permitted to make unapproved outbound calls, and staff actively refused at least one client's request to contact the Ombudsman.
|| R501-19-5(1)(a)-(b): Manager responsibilities and qualifications | Finding: The provider was out of compliance with R501-19-5(1)(b)((ii) and (iii) for not ensuring the manager has a bachelor's degree or equivalent training in a human service-related field and has at least three years management experience in a residential or secure treatment setting. During the investigation, a credential review revealed that eight (8) provider Program Managers do not meet the requirements for their position. || 26B-2-123(6)(a)-(b): Congregate care voice-to-voice communication | Finding: The provider was out of compliance with 26B-2-123(6)(a)(i) for failing to facilitate confidential voice-to-voice communication between a child and the child’s parents, guardian, foster parents, and siblings, as applicable. During the inspection, multiple client interviews confirmed that clients' weekly phone calls are conducted publicly and monitored by staff. The provider verified the practice, demonstrating that calls occur in a common area where staff remain within earshot to supervise the unit and are able to overhear conversations.
Inspection 4 Findings: R380-80-4(1): Provider shall protect each client | Finding: The provider was out of compliance with R380-80-4(1) for not protecting a client from mistreatment. During the inspection, video evidence showed a staff member grabbing the top of a client’s hair with his hand, bending his fingers around her hair at the root, and holding onto it in order to push the client’s head back and hold it in place.
